name: Wood Fired Sauna
notes:
Wood-fired sauna: the heat and water engine for the Tropical Spa Guild.
Thermal battery: stone walls and brick paving store the stove's heat and release it at night; schedule winter firings on forecast frost nights.
Water: the 4 × 4 m mini-roof sheds about 16 L per mm of rain into the beds below; mister and plunge runoff drains into the guild's damp pocket.
Loops: dry Blackbutt sawmill scraps fuel the stove; ash goes to the compost (with Ice Cream Bean leaves) before the beds; fresh cuts become mushroom logs; spent logs become hügel and compost.
Fire safety: keep a cleared, low-fuel ring around the sauna and woodpile, a spark arrestor on the flue, an extinguisher and hose at hand; no firing on total fire ban days.
The pad slopes down to the west; the mister is on the south side.
